title: Interleaved prefix hashset + GPU slab packing for cross-request prefix deduplication
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
We observe repeated prefix fragments across independent requests causing duplicated KV cache entries and GPU memory fragmentation. Existing dedupe approaches (coarse content-addressing or global prefix registries) either increase lookup latency under high QPS or cause heavy lock contention in the KV layer.

Goal:
1) Reduce duplicate KV entries stored on GPU across concurrent requests.
2) Reduce GPU slab fragmentation and total resident memory for long-lived models.
3) Keep per-request latency stable (no >5% P95 regression) and preserve throughput for continuous batching.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Interleaved Prefix Hashset: A lightweight, lock-free hashset stored on host memory that contains compact fingerprints (64-bit) of recent prefix fragments. During request intake, a fast host-side probe determines whether to reference an existing fragment in the GPU slab or materialize a new GPU fragment. This avoids expensive full-content lookups for the common case.
- Micro-batch-aware canonicalization: When requests enter continuous batching, the intake stage groups candidate fragments and canonicalizes them in a single pass across the micro-batch. This amortizes fingerprint checks and reduces duplicate GPU uploads.
- GPU Slab Packing: On the device we allocate slab-arenas with tight packing of fragment tensors (tokenized KV blocks) and a small relocation table. When canonicalization identifies duplicate fragments, the runtime links new references to existing slab ranges instead of copying tensors. Periodic compaction reclaims holes and coalesces small free ranges.
- Eviction/aging: Use a hybrid LRU+frequency sketch that runs on host to select slab pages for compaction or eviction. Eviction decisions are refreshed by the micro-batch coordinator to avoid removing entries reused within the same batch.

Operational constraints and trade-offs:
- Fingerprint collisions (64-bit) are extremely unlikely but not impossible. On collision detection (backend checksum mismatch) we fall back to materializing a separate fragment to preserve correctness and log an anomaly.
- Host hashset adds NVMe/hot-restart persistence later, but initial implementation will be in-process only to iterate quickly.
- Compaction is a background operation limited by a device occupancy budget to avoid interfering with serving SLOs.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Deduplication ratio: fraction of duplicate fragment references avoided. Target >= 35% for datasets with moderate template reuse (internal benchmark set).
- GPU resident memory reduction: target >= 20% reduction versus baseline for long-lived sessions.
- Latency impact: P95 regen <= +3% and throughput within +/-5%.
- CPU overhead: host probe must be <1% extra CPU per core under typical load.

Design artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PR-48012-interleaved-prefix-hashset
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2913
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-dedupe/interleaved-prefix-experiments

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged prototype on staging with small model (7B) and synthetic prefix-heavy traffic.
2) Canary on dedicated cluster with runtime-1.20 branch, limit to non-critical customer traffic.
3) Gradual ramp with telemetry (dedupe_ratio, compaction_time_ms, collision_count).
4) Global enable with automatic backoff if P95 or error rate exceeds threshold.

Risks and mitigation:
- Lock-free hashset correctness across threads: use well-tested folly/absl primitives and add stress tests under high concurrency.
- Compaction pause impacting inference: throttle compaction and test under realistic QPS patterns.
- Memory accounting complexity: add per-slab reference counters and deterministic accounting in the runtime to avoid leaks.

Next steps:
- Complete prototype PR changes for host-side fingerprint probe and slab link/unlink hooks (Marcus).
- Add unit tests for collision paths and relocation correctness (QA pairing requested).
- Create a short-run benchmark job for the internal eval harness (run by 2026-02-20).
